title: Oscar and the Wardrobe
premise: Odile Okonkwo, a night librarian who catalogs silences the way others catalog books, is asked by Eze, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, to become his final student. As she learns a tongue that exists only in one aging mind, she must also confront her own inheritance: an estranged mother's house slated for demolition, and the words they never said to each other. When Eze's health fails and the demolition date moves up, Odile realizes fluency requires not just vocabulary but confession. The novel ends with Odile speaking aloud — in both languages — a proper goodbye at her mother's empty house, recording it as the final entry in Eze's archive and the first entry in her own.
about_author: V. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging oral histories in coastal cities facing redevelopment. They write quietly devastating fiction about what survives when buildings, languages, and families do not.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet her on the night shift of the Meridian Library, where she keeps a private ledger of conversations she abandoned mid-sentence. Establishes her ritualized avoidance and the city's insomnia. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: A Man Who Speaks Alone
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An elderly man, Eze, begins visiting at 3 a.m., reading aloud in a language no one recognizes. She checks the catalog: the language has no other living speakers. He notices her listening. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking open routine.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Eze's POV. He formally asks Odile to become his last student, explaining he is dying and refuses to let the language die 'unwitnessed.' She hesitates; duty feels like a trap. Emotional beat: the terror of being chosen.

chapters.title: Lessons at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. First lessons among the stacks: greetings, names for rain, a word for grief that doubles as gratitude. Her ledger of unsaid things goes unopened for the first time in years. Emotional beat: tentative joy.

chapters.title: The House on Adeyemi Street
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A certified letter arrives: her estranged mother's house enters demolition proceedings, and Odile, as heir, must clear it within eight weeks. Flashbacks to the silence that split them. Emotional beat: dread resurfacing.

chapters.title: What the Wardrobe Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Clearing the house, she finds her childhood wardrobe locked from the inside — inside, her mother kept every letter Odile never sent, plus a dress made from fabric Odile once loved. Emotional beat: inheritance as ambush.

chapters.title: Eze's Grammar of Goodbye
chapters.summary: Eze's POV. He teaches the language's farewell constructions, which are elaborate, almost liturgical — goodbyes take days. He admits he never gave his own daughter a proper one. Emotional beat: mirrored regret.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The university's linguistics department learns of Eze and sends a team to 'optimize' the documentation — recordings, extraction, speed. Odile resents being sidelined as 'the emotional variable.' Emotional beat: love against institutional duty.

chapters.title: The Word That Has No Translation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Eze teaches a word meaning roughly 'the debt of things left unsaid.' She recognizes herself in it and, shaken, opens her old ledger for the first time since lessons began. Emotional beat: recognition without yet repentance.

chapters.title: Daughter, in Two Languages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Eze's estranged daughter arrives unexpectedly, hostile toward the project and toward Odile. Two daughters, two silences, one lesson room. Emotional beat: watching your own future argue with you.

chapters.title: Demolition Date Moved Up
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Bureaucratic error accelerates the demolition to three weeks. She must choose between finishing Eze's lessons and clearing the house. She tries to do both and fails at each. Emotional beat: the cost of divided duty.

chapters.title: The Recording Sessions
chapters.summary: Eze's POV. Under the linguists' lights, Eze's fluency falters; the language lives in conversation, not performance. Only sessions with Odile flow. The team leader privately concedes the method matters more than the data. Emotional beat: dignity defended.

chapters.title: Night Swim
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. After a failed session, Eze asks to see the sea one last time; they sneak out at dawn. He tells the story of his wife in the language, translating haltingly, and Odile understands most of it untranslated. Emotional beat: intimacy as comprehension.

chapters.title: The Locked Wardrobe, Opened
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She finally forces the wardrobe fully open and finds her mother's diary beneath the letters — pages showing her mother practiced saying sorry for years and never managed it either. Emotional beat: grief complicated by kinship.

chapters.title: Eze Collapses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Eze is hospitalized mid-lesson, leaving a sentence unfinished. His daughter blames Odile; the linguists propose machine transcription to finish the archive without him. Emotional beat: panic and possessiveness.

chapters.title: Stealing the Language
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile breaks protocol, smuggling a recorder into the hospital and continuing lessons at his bedside against medical advice and university rules. She accepts she may lose everything formal to keep something true. Emotional beat: commitment through transgression.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Turn
chapters.summary: Adaora's POV. Eze's daughter finds the recordings and hears her father telling stories she'd refused for thirty years. She sits down beside Odile, unprompted, and asks to be taught too. Emotional beat: reconciliation by proxy.

chapters.title: The Last Full Lesson
chapters.summary: Eze's POV. Knowing the end is near, Eze teaches the complete farewell rite — every phrase, every silence between phrases — and makes Odile and Adaora recite it to him while he can still hear. Emotional beat: rehearsal for loss.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Properly
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Eze dies at dawn; Odile performs the full farewell rite aloud over him, the language's last true conversation. The ward goes quiet. Emotional beat: devastation transfigured into ceremony.

chapters.title: The Empty House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On demolition eve, Odile stands in her mother's bare house and speaks the goodbye she owes — out loud, in English and in Eze's language — recording it into the archive. Adaora holds the recorder. Emotional beat: climax of confession.

chapters.title: Two Speakers
chapters.summary: Adaora's POV. At the archive's completion ceremony, the linguists note the language now has two speakers, not zero. Adaora and Odile converse briefly, publicly, in it. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled, identity rewritten.

chapters.title: The First Entry
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Months later, Odile closes her old ledger of unsaid things and opens a new notebook titled in Eze's language. The city still sleeps less every year, but she sleeps soundly after teaching her first student. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
